walkthroughs.title: Set up Maestro
walkthroughs.description: Go from a local CLI to a reviewed chat and Controlled Mutation without leaving VS Code.

steps.title: Install or locate Maestro CLI
steps.description: Install and configure the pinned CLI, then [show its binary identity](command:maestro.version).

steps.title: Verify the runtime
steps.description: [Run Maestro Doctor](command:maestro.doctor) and review the authoritative result in the terminal.

steps.title: Recover binary detection
steps.description: If detection fails, [open the binary path setting](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%22%40ext%3Aaxtonno.maestro-local-ai%20maestro.binaryPath%22).

steps.title: Chat about the active file
steps.description: Open a saved local file, then [start a focused chat](command:maestro.askActiveFile).

steps.title: Review a Controlled Mutation
steps.description: Select complete lines in a saved `app/*.php` file, then [preview a mutation](command:maestro.replaceSelection).

maestro.binaryPath.markdownDescription: Optional Maestro executable path in the current extension-host environment. Default: empty. Example: `/home/me/.local/bin/maestro` in Remote WSL. An explicit path takes precedence over that host's exact `PATH`. Configure it independently per local or remote machine; relative paths resolve from the selected workspace. A binary installed only on the UI host is never used remotely.

maestro.configPath.markdownDescription: Optional Maestro v4 configuration file in the current extension-host environment. Default: empty. Example: `./maestro.yaml`. An explicit workspace-contained path takes precedence; when empty, the remote or local CLI uses its own `MAESTRO_CONFIG`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, then `~/.config/maestro/config.yaml` as created by `maestro setup`.

enumDescriptions: Qualified two-model profile: qwen3.5:9b for chat and qwen2.5-coder:14b for Controlled Mutation.
maestro.profile.markdownDescription: Expected Maestro product profile for this workspace. The CLI-reported effective profile remains authoritative. The rejected single-model evaluation profile is not available.

maestro.terminalName.description: Name used for the dedicated integrated terminal.
